# The block kit

**This file is generated.** Run `node scripts/write-block-kit-doc.mjs` after changing
the manifest, the material families or the collider definitions. Every number below is
read from `Assets/Art/Blocks/block_asset_manifest.json`, from `src/blocks/`, and from
the conversion report, so it cannot drift from the code.

One Structural Unit, written SU, is one metre. Model axes are X width, Y up, Z depth.
That convention comes from the art pass, in `Assets/Art/Blocks/README.md`, and is
adopted unchanged as the game world unit so the project has exactly one scale.

Mass is volume times the family density, which is what Rapier computes from the same
two numbers. Compound colliders sum their parts without subtracting overlaps, so the
cross beam and the stabiliser read slightly heavy here.

## Pivots, and why they matter

Thirteen pieces are authored with a **center-bottom** pivot: the origin sits on the base
and the geometry runs upward, so placing one at `y: 3` puts its underside at 3 SU.
Two pieces use a **geometric-center** pivot, where the origin is in the middle of the
bounding box:

- `A03_CROSS_BEAM`, Cross Beam. Placing one at `y: 3` puts its underside at 1.5 SU and its top at 4.5 SU.
- `A04_ROLLER`, Roller. Placing one at `y: 3` puts its underside at 2.5 SU and its top at 3.5 SU.

Rapier colliders are always centred on their own origin, so a center-bottom piece needs
its collider lifted by half its height and a geometric-center piece needs no lift at
all. `src/blocks/colliders.js` computes that as `pivotLift`. Getting it wrong sinks
pieces halfway into the ground, and it looks like a physics bug rather than a placement
one, which is why the unit suite checks every piece.

## Material families

| Family | Density (kg/SU³) | Restitution | Friction | Hit points (J) | Score weight |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Wood | 150 | 0.16 | 0.62 | 280,000 | 1 |
| Brick | 300 | 0.1 | 0.78 | 400,000 | 1.4 |
| Stone | 400 | 0.08 | 0.84 | 620,000 | 1.8 |
| Concrete | 350 | 0.09 | 0.8 | 500,000 | 1.6 |
| Steel | 520 | 0.22 | 0.5 | 1,100,000 | 2.4 |
| Painted Steel | 470 | 0.2 | 0.54 | 800,000 | 2.1 |
| Rubber | 190 | 0.72 | 0.9 | 700,000 | 1.2 |

**The densities are not the real densities of the materials they are named after.** Real
steel is 7850 kg per cubic metre, which makes a 1 SU cube weigh nearly eight tonnes and
immovable by any ball a child would believe in. These values keep the ordering and the
feel while compressing the range to roughly three to one, so every family is movable and
heavy things still feel heavy. A deliberate game value, not a mistake about physics.

**Hit points are joules of accumulated impact energy**, set against the impact energies
this game actually produces rather than guessed. See `docs/DECISIONS.md` D-007 for the
measurement: a standing structure produces contacts under 10 J, while a square ball hit
is worth 5,000 to 50,000 J.

Generated by `scripts/convert-blocks.mjs` against three r185, from Assets/Art/Blocks/MaterialVariants/V2 (V2 materialized variants).

**15 of 15 pieces** match the manifest on width, height, depth and pivot within 1 mm.

| ID | Measured W x H x D (SU) | Measured min Y | Triangles | Draw calls | Was |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `B01_SMALL_BLOCK` | 1 x 1 x 1 | 0 | 108 | 2 | 72 |
| `B02_MEDIUM_BLOCK` | 2 x 1 x 1 | 0 | 108 | 2 | 72 |
| `B03_LONG_BEAM` | 4 x 1 x 1 | 0 | 108 | 2 | 72 |
| `B04_TALL_BLOCK` | 1 x 3 x 1 | 0 | 108 | 1 | 1 |
| `B05_LARGE_BLOCK` | 2 x 2 x 1 | 0 | 108 | 1 | 1 |
| `S01_ROUND_COLUMN` | 1 x 3 x 1 | 0 | 380 | 2 | 261 |
| `S02_SHORT_COLUMN` | 1 x 2 x 1 | 0 | 108 | 1 | 1 |
| `S03_WIDE_FOOTING` | 3 x 0.5 x 1 | 0 | 108 | 1 | 1 |
| `S04_WEDGE` | 2 x 1 x 1 | 0 | 80 | 2 | 32 |
| `S05_ARCH` | 3 x 2 x 1 | 0 | 220 | 1 | 1 |
| `A01_T_BLOCK` | 3 x 2 x 1 | 0 | 220 | 2 | 33 |
| `A02_L_BLOCK` | 2 x 2 x 1 | 0 | 164 | 2 | 57 |
| `A03_CROSS_BEAM` | 3 x 3 x 1 | -1.5 | 332 | 2 | 92 |
| `A04_ROLLER` | 2 x 1 x 1 | -0.5 | 380 | 2 | 261 |
| `A05_MECHANICAL_STABILIZER` | 3 x 2 x 1 | 0 | 3028 | 5 | 84 |

The last two columns are draw calls after and before merging material groups. The
authored meshes assign materials face by face, leaving as many as 261 geometry groups
on a single column, and every group becomes its own glTF primitive. Merging by
material is the difference between 261 draw calls per column and 2.

## What the FBX files do not carry

The V2 materialized FBX files carry material **names** and per face material
**assignment**, but no appearance at all. Every material in all fifteen files reads back
as `MeshPhongMaterial` with colour `#cccccc`, no texture and no useful specular. The V2
look was authored as procedural Blender node materials, which FBX cannot carry, which is
why `Art/Materials/V2/V2_MATERIAL_LIBRARY.blend` exists.

So appearance is rebuilt in code, in `src/render/materials.js`, keyed to the same twelve
authored material names, with colours read off the V2 preview renders. The per face
assignment the FBX did preserve is what makes it work: end grain still lands on the ends
of a beam because the art said so. This is an approximation of the approved art
direction, not the direction itself.
